title: VPC post-deploy sanity wave: orchestrated API & model smoke sweep
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an orchestrated 'sanity wave' runner that executes a deterministic sequence of post-deploy checks for Private (VPC) deployments. The runner will be invoked automatically at the end of our Terraform apply pipeline (and optionally from the Console 'Run checks' button) and must validate: 1) API readiness (auth handshake, routing, TLS), 2) model instantiation and low-concurrency load tests (validate model can accept requests, KV cache warming path), 3) smoke tests for core endpoints (chat/generate, embeddings, health endpoints), 4) basic SLO guardrails (latency/correctness thresholds) and 5) create a summarized verdict posted to the deployment dashboard and to the deployment incident channel. The goal is to fail fast for customer-impacting regressions and provide actionable logs, links to artifacts, and remediation hints for on-call/SEs.
acceptance_criteria: Runner is triggered automatically by infra CI artifact post-apply and can be run manually from the console/CLI
API readiness check passes for control-plane and data-plane endpoints (TLS + token + 200 /health) within 60s
Model load test: single-instance model can load and respond to a 16-token prompt with p95 latency < 2s in the smoke sweep environment
Smoke endpoint tests (chat, embeddings, reranking) return syntactically valid responses and match regression prompt golden outputs >= 95% token-level similarity threshold
Runner outputs a single JSON verdict artifact (s3) and posts a human-friendly summary to the deployment dashboard and Slack channel
Failure modes are triaged into actionable buckets (config, infra, model, auth) and map to suggested follow-ups in the UI
test_plan: Create small synthetic deployment in staging vpc-qa and instrument with verbose logs
Wire CI/CD: infra repo Github Actions job 'sanity-wave-run' runs after 'terraform apply' and uploads verdict to s3://redwood-postdeploy-artifacts/<deploy-id>/sanity-wave.json
Run model-load in isolation then repeat with 2x concurrency to validate graceful degradation paths
Compare outputs of smoke prompts against stored golden responses in CI using fuzzy token-level diff (tool: evals-lite)
Record metrics to test dashboard: api_up(percentage), p95_latency_ms, model_load_time_ms, kvcache_warm_hits
runbook_steps: Step 0: On deploy completion, identify deploy-id from terraform outputs and trigger sanity-wave-run job
Step 1: API readiness: curl --fail --header 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' https://<api-host>/v1/health && curl /v1/models to validate catalog
Step 2: Model load smoke: run small harness (tools/sanity_wave/load_model.py) with flags --model <model> --prompt-file smoke/prompts.json --max-concurrency 1
Step 3: Functional smoke: hit /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings with golden prompts and validate structure and tokens
Step 4: Metrics collection: push p95 latency, success_rate, model_load_time to CI metrics bucket and wait for 30s aggregation window
Step 5: Verdict: aggregate checks, generate human-readable summary and JSON artifact, upload to s3, and post Slack summary to #deployments-vpc
Step 6: On failure: run 'sanity_wave --diagnose' which attaches logs, last-10 requests, and suggested remediation checklist to the verdict artifact
updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed for model-load harness — initial python runner prototype can instantiate a quantized model and run a 16-token prompt. Found a race when kv cache warmup overlaps with autoscaler spin-up; added a 5s jitter before first request.

2026-02-28: Design review with PM and SRE — agreed to require both API health + model smoke to pass before marking a deploy as 'ready'. PM requested a manual override flow for emergencies (will be gated by ACL in Console).
2026-03-03: Infra PR #1248 opened with GitHub Actions job and S3 artifact upload. Requested review from @sre-team. Linked to infra module outputs for api_endpoint and model_endpoint.

2026-03-06: Security review note — token used by CI job must be limited to 'sanity-wave:run' and cannot access customer data buckets. Updated terraform module to provision a scoped CI service account (PR comment: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1248#issuecomment-5421).
2026-03-09: Added improved failure categories in the runner: AUTH, ROUTING, MODEL_LOAD, TIMEOUT, UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE. Each category maps to a top-level remediation link in the verdict summary.

2026-03-10: Running in staging for 48h; two transient model_load TIMEOUTs observed during concurrent deploys — mitigated by adding a circuit-breaker to pause sanity-wave and retry with backoff when cluster is scaling. Post-deploy metric dashboard panel created.
Next: finish UI button to trigger manual re-run and add golden prompt set for embeddings; target close by 2026-03-15.
notes: Trade-off: we keep the sanity-wave lightweight (small prompt set, short windows) to avoid large cost and to reduce false positives. Deeper QA (longer load tests, large concurrency) is captured in separate runbooks (ENG-198341).
Decision: Runner will treat KV cache priming as a soft-failure (warning) unless subsequent model responses exceed latency thresholds — reduces flakiness during autoscaler events.
Follow-up: add a 'dry-run' mode that simulates model slowdowns to validate alerting and on-call playbooks (owner: @sre-team).
Reminder: ensure any artifacts in s3 are TTL'd (30 days) to comply with retention policy and avoid leaking sensitive prompts.
